description: Returns what classic search actually sent this site over the reported window: total times shown, visits, click rate and impression-weighted average rank, plus the top searches people used and the top pages they landed on. Numbers are the engine's own — Google Search Console and/or Bing Webmaster Tools, whichever the owner connected — never estimated, and never blended (the two count different searchers). Use it to answer "how is this site doing in search?". Returns source="" when no engine has reported yet. When source="bing", totals come from Bing's site-wide daily series (sample sums until that series has reported) while topQueries and topPages are its top-N sample counted separately — the lists sum to less than the totals, and one busy page can even out-count a tile. Neither is an error: state the split rather than reconciling the numbers.

source.description: Which engine to read: "google" or "bing". Omit for the richer one that has data.

name: agentimus-read-search-performance

pages.description: Pages the engine attributed traffic to — topPages is only the largest few.

queries.description: Distinct searches in the window — topQueries is only the largest few of these.

daily.description: Clicks and impressions per day, oldest first — Google from Search Console's date split, Bing from its site-wide daily traffic report. History accumulates locally beyond each engine's own window; the payload ships the most recent 112 days.

impressions.description: Times shown in Google Discover this window — a feed, not a search; most sites honestly sit at 0.

start.description: Y-m-d, first day of the reported window.

source.description: The engine these numbers came from; empty when none has data yet.

dropped.description: Rows the last poll could not store, because the snapshot keeps only its busiest N. What is missing is the quiet tail — say so rather than treating the stored set as everything.

pageCap.description: Always 0 now: Bing is worked through a few pages per poll until every page has been asked about, so no page sits permanently outside anything.

dropped.description: Rows the last poll could not store, because the snapshot keeps only its busiest N. The engines report clicks-descending, so what is missing is the quiet tail — say so rather than treating the stored set as everything.

pageCap.description: Always 0: no source samples a fixed set of pages any more. Kept so readers that branch on it keep taking their no-sampling path.

postId.description: 0 when the URL maps to no post (an archive, a removed page).

isProbe.description: True when this is a search-operator probe, not a person's search.

clicks.description: Visits that came from those appearances.

impressions.description: Times a page of this site appeared in results.

position.description: Impression-weighted average rank; 1 is the top result.

probeShare.description: Percentage of these impressions that came from search-operator probes (site:, intext:) run by scrapers rather than people. Nothing is subtracted — these are the engine's own totals — but a high share means the click rate above understates how people actually respond. Say so before drawing conclusions from it.

updatedAt.description: Unix time the daily series last refreshed successfully; 0 = never. Older than a few days = the trend is last-good data, not current — say so.

ready.description: True only when 14 days of history exist — before that a week-on-week claim would be a guess, so the numbers below stay zero and mean NOTHING.

title: Get classic-search performance
